Every internal conversation at Rogo is recorded and fed into a company brain called Shrek.

"When anyone starts, we say, "Hey, just FYI, you're always being recorded." 

There's a dashboard where you can see the swamp of everything that people are working on at any given time, but it's connected to all of our different systems. 

It can shape every answer and deliverable that way, and it's both proactive and reactive. 

Someone can go in and say, I'm trying to get up to speed on how I should talk about model routing and how I should think about the value prop there for a very large institution and what the savings will be, and it can pull out all that information for you."

I recently shared the sBTC loop I’ve been running on @ZestProtocol.

But I forgot to mention their new Bitcoin Collateral Vaults product.

Zest already has $75M+ TVL and 800+ BTC deposited, so it’s looking quite strong. This new feature is a meaningful shift from lending on Stacks to building around native BTC itself.

It’s a very simple model:

→ Keep native $BTC self-custodied on Bitcoin
→ Borrow $USDC against it
→ Access liquidity from chains where it already exists

The product is already live as a capped mainnet demo using real BTC + real USDC, with limits on how much BTC can be used as collateral.

I also compared the current UX with Babylon. I noticed that Babylon’s flow has more setup and signing steps before the vault is usable.

In comparison, opening a Zest collateral vault is much simpler and faster.

IMO, it should be a nice step forward for BTC-backed lending. Definitely keeping an eye on $ZEST for the next few weeks.

Disclosure: I’m a $ZEST holder.

I already posted about @stealfxyz building a product that lets you use crypto without exposing your entire wallet activity.

Well, they've just released a beta version of the app.

Now you can test the product out for yourself:

• Install the TestFlight app
• Go to the link provided in the QT
• Install the Stealf app
• Create an account
• Deposit a few dollars in SOL or USDC (only from Solana)
• Go to "Private Balance"
• Register your SOL/USDC (@UmbraPrivacy powers the private balance)

Now, your Private Balance is completely separate from your Public Balance. No one can link the two.

Also, the Private Balance doesn't require KYC. You can use it the same way as your public balance for staking, xStocks, or buying gift cards, with Visa cards coming later this year.

It really is one of the most innovative privacy-focused crypto products I’ve found lately.

Seeing myself becoming a heavy user once it's out of beta.

#Uranium #Silver #Copper #Gold

Daily Metals Pulse — September 23, 2026

The Fed’s higher-for-longer message is keeping pressure on gold and silver, but the bigger structural stories remain intact.

☢️ Uranium: The U.S. is pushing to accelerate domestic enrichment as nuclear demand rises, driven increasingly by AI and data-center power needs. Supply security is becoming a strategic priority.

🥈 Silver: Short-term pressure from high rates and solar thrifting, but AI infrastructure, electronics and EV demand are helping offset weaker silver use per solar panel. The market remains structurally tight.

🟠 Copper: Up for a sixth consecutive session as supply shortages collide with demand from power grids, data centers and AI. Tariff-related stockpiling is adding further pressure to available supply.

🥇 Gold: Pulling back as traders price higher interest rates and a stronger dollar. But persistent inflation, geopolitical risk and rising government debt continue to support the long-term case.

The common theme is clear: the world is demanding more electricity, more infrastructure and more strategic metals—while new mine and fuel-supply capacity remains slow, expensive and politically difficult to build.

That imbalance has not gone away.

tweets.text:
You'll spend 3 hours researching a token.

Then 3 seconds deciding how much to buy.

The second decision is the one that wipes people out.

Here's the simple framework I use to size every position:

1. Decide how much you're okay losing first.

Say you have a $50K portfolio.

You find a token you like. If the trade goes wrong, you're okay losing 2% of the portfolio. So your max loss is $1,000.

You buy at $2.50 and decide you'll sell if it drops to $1.50. That's a 40% drop.

So: $1,000 ÷ 40% = $2,500 position.

You put $2,500 in. If it falls 40% and you exit, you lose $1,000. Not a cent more.

2. You don't need to buy everything at once.

This is where most people mess up.

They find something they like and put the full amount in immediately.

Instead, start small. Maybe you're comfortable putting $2,500 in eventually. Start with $800 to $1,000.

If the project keeps doing what you expected and price moves your way, add more. If you were wrong, you found out with a small position instead of taking the full hit.

3. Think about what happens BEFORE the token hits your target.

Maybe you think something eventually does 3x. Alrighty, cool.

But can you handle it dropping 20% first?

Can you hold if nothing happens for two months?

Can you sit through a few ugly red days without panicking?

Being right eventually doesn't help if your position is so big that you sell on the first dip.

4. If a position is stressing you out, it's too big.

If you're checking the chart every 10 minutes, losing sleep, moving your stop, or your mood swings every time the token moves…

Reduce the size and you'll sleep way better.

You should be able to be wrong without it ruining your week. That's the biggest thing I've learned about position sizing.

Bear markets don't take people out of the game. The first few bullish months do, because that's when everyone quietly doubles their size and stops thinking about the downside.

Go smaller than your gut tells you.

Jensen Huang Calls Out AI Doomers: “All of These Predictions Have Been Wrong”

@chamath:

“What does that mean, 10% chance of extinction?”

@JensenHuang:

“It's made up, and it shouldn't be done. It's irresponsible.

Now, the fact of the matter is, let's go back and look at the real facts.

There was a prediction that in five years' time, radiology will be completely taken over by artificial intelligence and there'll be no radiologists in the world. That has proven to be exactly the opposite. We need more radiologists than ever in the world. However, AI has taken over radiology completely, which is great. It has automated scan reading, which is great.

There was a prediction that within 6-12 months, 90% of code would already be generated by AI. That has turned out to be wrong.

Within 6-9 months, that was predicted last year, 50% of entry jobs will be wiped out. That has proven to be wrong. What else has proven to be wrong? I mean, all of these predictions have been wrong.”

@DavidSacks:

“GPT-2 would be too unsafe to release, that LLaMA-3 would be too unsafe to release.”

@Jason:

“Half of white collar jobs would be gone next year.”

Sacks:

“The jobs apocalypse, yeah.”

Jensen:

“We have to take accountability. We have to take account for all of the stupid predictions that were made. Somebody has to take (accountability).

And, and so we ought to just keep track of all that, and of course, people do, and remind us that those, those predictions are inconsistent with, ultimately, America winning the AI race.”

Theres no growing out of debt at these levels, so governments have no choice but to print to pay the interest and borrow more on top.

One thing I’ve been coming to terms with is how there is no objective truth in markets. 

If you’re a naturally bullish person you interpret signs of euphoria as signs of adoption and justified optimism. You extrapolate good conditions perpetually. 

If you’re a natural bear you read the exact same signs as omens to the implosion that comes with every bubble, grow indignant in richly valued markets, think everything is a grift. Your mind subtly overweights anything that smells bearish. 

Everyone’s just talking over each other most of the time.
